Idea.Title: Prefer the official GitHub CLI packages (Debian/RPM/Homebrew) — they’re the supported install path
Idea.Description: The strongest editorial story the source supports is that GitHub CLI provides official packages (Debian, RPM, Homebrew) that are explicitly maintained by the CLI maintainers and updated via a CI deployment workflow — and these are the recommended, supported installation methods.
Idea.Audience: Developers, sysadmins, and package-maintenance teams who must choose a reliable, supported way to install gh across Linux and macOS.
Idea.Rationale: Why it matters: The source repeatedly labels Debian, RPM and Homebrew packages as "supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers" and states updates are powered by the project's deployment workflow. That makes a clear, actionable editorial angle: explain to readers that these installs are the officially supported routes and what that support means in practice (updates come from the maintainers, packaging hosted on the marketing site/formulae). Gaps and uncertainty: the source does not provide comparative data on update frequency, security auditing, or specific SLAs versus community packages — so any deeper claims about timeliness or security would be interpretive and must be framed as such.
Idea.Evidence: Explicit statements: "Debian packages are hosted on the GitHub CLI marketing site... These packages are supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers with updates powered by [GitHub CLI deployment workflow]." Homebrew: "The GitHub CLI formulae is supported by the GitHub CLI maintainers..." RPM: similar language for RPM packages. The source provides install commands for these official methods (apt/dnf/brew).
